evidence.claim: Direct Cloud Run IAP protects all ingress traffic before the container; a before-login intro must be outside that protected service.
Cloud Run permits public access scoped to one service using allUsers invoker authorization, independently of another IAP service.
Firebase Hosting serves static files over HTTPS and can link to the protected app.
Effective project policies permit all ingress, public IAM members and service-account creation. No additional policy exception is required for the Cloud Run candidate.
evidence.source: Local private policy readback, 2026-11-20; five effective constraints examined

evidence.claim: In this project Cloud Run is already enabled and has a working image build, scan, KMS signature/provenance and owner-only deployment path. Firebase Management and Hosting APIs are absent among 64 enabled APIs. Candidate A extends the existing release path with one service and a no-grant identity; candidate B additionally requires Firebase project onboarding and a static deployment path. This comparison concerns platform changes only, not cost or runtime security superiority.
Adding Firebase enables additional APIs and service accounts; it cannot be fully undone and requires Firebase terms acceptance.

flip_conditions: A pre-existing approved Firebase hosting project and equivalent static release controls become available.
Measured public landing cost or cold-start behavior fails an agreed target and a static-hosting trial demonstrates an advantage.
The public Cloud Run isolation or authorization smoke tests fail, or deploying it would require broader project security changes.

options.description: Separate public Cloud Run landing entrypoint using the existing signed image pipeline; dedicated no-grant runtime identity, no storage configuration, fixed intro and sign-in redirect only. Protected app remains IAP-enabled.
Add Firebase to the existing project and deploy a separate static HTTPS intro linking to the unchanged IAP app. Introduce a static-file release path.

requirements.text: Before sign-in: public intro, protected app
Every signed-in visitor sees all active users masked emails
Keep protected app owner-only and invitations on hold until explicit approval

requirements.source: Workspace operating directives: simplicity and surgical changes
requirements.text: Prefer a small extension of the existing verified release and security controls; avoid unrelated platform changes
Preserve hardened image, SBOM/scan, signature, provenance, least privilege, restricted egress and WORM deployment audit controls where applicable
Incremental public-page traffic and monthly billed cost; existing planning target is USD 10/month, not an enforced cap

validation_before_release: Anonymous intro returns 200 without identity content
Sign-in redirects only to the configured protected app
Public service has no review/upload/user-list endpoints or storage grants
Protected app keeps IAP and owner-only IAM
Two synthetic verified identities see masked activity but isolated chat/preferences
Scan, signature and provenance pass on the deployed image
